text.approach: Reached via a multi-day backpack up the Thunder Creek Trail from Colonial Creek Campground to Park Creek Pass (roughly 40 miles round trip with on the order of 7,000 ft of cumulative gain including the bonus climb to Junction Camp), or as part of a Ptarmigan-style traverse linking Cascade Pass/Buckner/Park Creek Pass. From a Park Creek Pass-area camp, it is a short day-trip scramble up to the Booker-Buckner col and on to the summit.

text.approach: Start from the end of Forest Service road 4096 and follow the Bedal Creek trail, which is rough and blown down in places. Where the tread is lost in a rocky creek bed, keep going up the creek through one short wet step until the path reappears on the right. The trail fades in the heather beneath the southwest face of Sloan; from the basin there, climb about a thousand feet south to the ridge crest. Drop on grassy, rocky ground to the small tarn often called Cadet Lake, cross over Heineken Peak, and go down its steep grassy gullies to a low point near 5,600 ft above the remnant Mayflower Glacier. The route starts there, on the ridge rising on the northeast side of Cadet Peak toward a small hanging glacier.
text.overview: A high alpine ridge traverse linking Sloan Peak to Cadet Peak's northeast ridge and face, following the timberline crest between the two mountains rather than a direct up-and-down approach to Cadet alone.
text.descent: Cross the summit plateau and come down the standard route toward Glacier Basin. The upper cliff band is the tricky part when you did not climb the standard line: follow cairns and look for the worn boot path through it. Lower down a tunnel through the brush leads into Glacier Basin. The whole descent is steep and loose, hard on the knees, but not technical. From the basin pick up the Glacier Basin
